metadata.name: Harbor Desk synthetic repository reading checks
metadata.description: Twelve hand-authored, exact-answer repository/configuration reading tasks. All cases share the same complete synthetic repository prefix, including plausible inactive configuration distractors. These are transparent local smoke checks, not a validated or hidden benchmark.
metadata.context_token_count_note: No tokenizer or model was invoked to build this fixture. Record prompt_eval_count from the tested runtime; token length depends on its tokenizer and chat template.
metadata.suggested_answer_instruction: Read the supplied repository snapshot and answer the question. Output only the requested concise answer. Do not include reasoning, explanation, labels, quotation marks, Markdown, or code fences.

steps: Collapse all internal whitespace runs to one ASCII space
recommended_normalization.comparison: Exact case-sensitive equality of normalized response text and normalized expected_answer. Do not strip punctuation, units, code fences or explanatory prose, and do not use a model judge. Case is preserved because paths, identifiers and configuration strings can be case-sensitive.

limitations: All cases concern a single short fictional repository, so the twelve outcomes are correlated and do not measure broad coding or production-agent capability.
Answers and examples are public in this fixture; use them as development smoke checks, not as an unseen holdout after tuning on them.
Exact formatting compliance contributes to the score. Preserve raw outputs to distinguish formatting failures from factual failures.
The fixture alone does not validate KV compression, cache eviction, memory savings, or any serving-policy improvement.
Repeated common prefixes can support a runtime prefix-reuse experiment only if cache reuse and timing are observed separately; identical prompt text is not proof of reuse.

# Harbor Desk repository snapshot

This is a fictional repository fixture for a ticket-processing service, release 0.8.3. Every name, tenant, bucket, path, and value below is synthetic. The snapshot is complete for the questions: do not assume settings from another release or from a real product.

## README.md — active configuration

The running environment is production. There are no command-line overrides, deployment-injected overrides, or unlisted environment variables. Build the effective configuration by starting with config/default.yaml, recursively merging config/production.yaml, and finally recursively merging the selected tenant's overrides from config/tenants.yaml. A later leaf value replaces an earlier leaf value; an absent key inherits its previous value. Boolean false is an explicit value and is never treated as a missing setting. Tenant identity fields such as region, plan, and suspended are read directly from the tenant record; they are not configuration overrides.

Files under archive/ are historical examples and are not loaded. Files under tests/ describe test-only values and are not loaded in production. docs/operations.md describes monitoring policy and does not override configuration. All durations explicitly use the units written in the setting name. Counts and limits are integers. Configured retries count the first attempt: max_attempts=4 means at most four total calls, with at most three waits between them.

The current deployment runs one general worker per tenant. Workers use the tenant plan's max_inflight directly; there is no multiplication by replica count. Export worker settings apply only if a question explicitly names an export worker. The examples in this snapshot use no dynamic autoscaling.

## config/default.yaml

service:
  name: harbor-desk
  listen_port: 8080
  request_timeout_ms: 2000
  health_timeout_ms: 250
worker:
  heartbeat_interval_s: 15
  shutdown_grace_s: 40
  max_poll_items: 64
retention:
  audit_days: 30
  local_log_days: 3
queues:
  standard: tickets.standard
  priority: tickets.urgent
  quarantine: tickets.quarantine
retry:
  max_attempts: 4
  initial_delay_s: 1
  multiplier: 2
upload:
  max_chunk_items: 16
  max_document_bytes: 1048576
features:
  audit: true
  webhooks: true
  preview_exports: false

## config/production.yaml

service:
  listen_port: 8443
  request_timeout_ms: 1800
retention:
  audit_days: 21
worker:
  shutdown_grace_s: 60
dispatch:
  dedup_window_s: 90
features:
  webhooks: false

## config/tenants.yaml

cedar:
  region: eu
  plan: team
  suspended: false
  overrides:
    retention:
      audit_days: 7
    features:
      webhooks: true
birch:
  region: us
  plan: pro
  suspended: false
  overrides:
    retry:
      max_attempts: 5
spruce:
  region: eu
  plan: free
  suspended: true
  overrides:
    retention:
      audit_days: 3
    service:
      request_timeout_ms: 1200

## config/regions.yaml

eu:
  deployment_region: eu-west-2
  audit_bucket: harbor-prod-eu-audit
  export_bucket: harbor-prod-eu-exports
  attachment_bucket: harbor-prod-eu-files
  metrics_prefix: hd.eu
us:
  deployment_region: us-central-1
  audit_bucket: harbor-prod-us-audit
  export_bucket: harbor-prod-us-exports
  attachment_bucket: harbor-prod-us-files
  metrics_prefix: hd.us

Audit records go to regions[tenant.region].audit_bucket. Export objects go to the export_bucket in the same region. Attachments use attachment_bucket. The deployment_region string is metadata, not a key into a second routing table. Bucket names are logical names in this fixture and cannot be contacted.

## config/plans.yaml

free:
  max_inflight: 3
  monthly_export_limit: 10
  attachment_limit_mb: 5
team:
  max_inflight: 8
  monthly_export_limit: 100
  attachment_limit_mb: 25
pro:
  max_inflight: 12
  monthly_export_limit: 500
  attachment_limit_mb: 50

A tenant's general-worker concurrency limit is plans[tenant.plan].max_inflight. The optional export worker has its own fixed concurrency of 2 and does not change the general-worker limit. The monthly export limit is a billing counter, not a concurrency setting. A suspended tenant remains in the configuration but cannot dispatch new work.

## src/dispatch.py

def classify_ticket(score, tier, flagged):
    if flagged:
        return "quarantine"
    if tier == "free" and score >= 90:
        return "manual"
    if score >= 80:
        return "priority"
    return "standard"

def webhook_enabled(tenant, effective_config):
    return effective_config["features"]["webhooks"] and not tenant["suspended"]

def route_for(classification, effective_config):
    if classification == "manual":
        return "tickets.manual-review"
    return effective_config["queues"][classification]

The classifier returns a classification, not a queue name. route_for runs afterward. Scores are numbers on a 0–100 scale with no rounding. Webhook enablement is independent of audit.

## src/retry.py

def retry_delays(max_attempts, initial_delay_s, multiplier):
    return [
        initial_delay_s * (multiplier ** i)
        for i in range(max_attempts - 1)
    ]

The caller waits after each failed call except the last. There is no initial wait, jitter, or final wait. If every attempt fails, each returned delay is used once. Execution time is separate from waiting time.

## src/ingest.py

def split_batches(items, max_chunk_items):
    return [
        items[start:start + max_chunk_items]
        for start in range(0, len(items), max_chunk_items)
    ]

def canonical_path(path):
    while path != "/" and path.endswith("/"):
        path = path[:-1]
    return path

Batching retains the final partial batch and neither filters nor duplicates items. canonical_path only removes trailing slashes while preserving a root slash; it does not decode URLs or change internal slashes.

## src/http.py

def timeout_for(route, effective_config):
    if route == "/readyz":
        return effective_config["service"]["health_timeout_ms"]
    if route.startswith("/exports/"):
        return 9000
    return effective_config["service"]["request_timeout_ms"]

The caller passes the canonical path to timeout_for. Health checks use /readyz. Export paths use the fixed timeout in this function. Other paths inherit request_timeout_ms from the merged configuration. The selected timeout is an integer number of milliseconds; this function does not start a timer or perform network I/O.

## docs/operations.md — reference notes

The dashboard warns after three missed heartbeat intervals; that threshold is not the interval. A developer reverse proxy can listen on 9443, but it is outside production. Audit retention is independent of local logs. The billing export limit is not a concurrency limit. Paid plans do not automatically enable webhooks. Export workers start only for export jobs.

## tests/test_settings.py — test-only overrides

TEST_SETTINGS = {
    "service": {"listen_port": 9090, "request_timeout_ms": 50},
    "worker": {"heartbeat_interval_s": 1},
    "retention": {"audit_days": 1},
    "upload": {"max_chunk_items": 4},
}

These test values are injected by the unit-test runner only. None are used by the production snapshot.

  listen_port: 9443
worker:
  heartbeat_interval_s: 20
retention:
  audit_days: 14
queues:
  priority: tickets.high
retry:
  max_attempts: 3
upload:
  max_chunk_items: 8

The historical file is inactive. No queue aliases are defined. Questions concern the active snapshot unless they explicitly name an archived or test file.

This is a fictional repository fixture for a ticket-processing service, release 0.8.3. Every name, tenant, bucket, path, and value below is synthetic. The snapshot is complete for the questions: do not assume settings from another release or from a real product.

## README.md — active configuration

The running environment is production. There are no command-line overrides, deployment-injected overrides, or unlisted environment variables. Build the effective configuration by starting with config/default.yaml, recursively merging config/production.yaml, and finally recursively merging the selected tenant's overrides from config/tenants.yaml. A later leaf value replaces an earlier leaf value; an absent key inherits its previous value. Boolean false is an explicit value and is never treated as a missing setting. Tenant identity fields such as region, plan, and suspended are read directly from the tenant record; they are not configuration overrides.

Files under archive/ are historical examples and are not loaded. Files under tests/ describe test-only values and are not loaded in production. docs/operations.md describes monitoring policy and does not override configuration. All durations explicitly use the units written in the setting name. Counts and limits are integers. Configured retries count the first attempt: max_attempts=4 means at most four total calls, with at most three waits between them.

The current deployment runs one general worker per tenant. Workers use the tenant plan's max_inflight directly; there is no multiplication by replica count. Export worker settings apply only if a question explicitly names an export worker. The examples in this snapshot use no dynamic autoscaling.

## config/default.yaml

service:
  name: harbor-desk
  listen_port: 8080
  request_timeout_ms: 2000
  health_timeout_ms: 250
worker:
  heartbeat_interval_s: 15
  shutdown_grace_s: 40
  max_poll_items: 64
retention:
  audit_days: 30
  local_log_days: 3
queues:
  standard: tickets.standard
  priority: tickets.urgent
  quarantine: tickets.quarantine
retry:
  max_attempts: 4
  initial_delay_s: 1
  multiplier: 2
upload:
  max_chunk_items: 16
  max_document_bytes: 1048576
features:
  audit: true
  webhooks: true
  preview_exports: false

## config/production.yaml

service:
  listen_port: 8443
  request_timeout_ms: 1800
retention:
  audit_days: 21
worker:
  shutdown_grace_s: 60
dispatch:
  dedup_window_s: 90
features:
  webhooks: false

## config/tenants.yaml

cedar:
  region: eu
  plan: team
  suspended: false
  overrides:
    retention:
      audit_days: 7
    features:
      webhooks: true
birch:
  region: us
  plan: pro
  suspended: false
  overrides:
    retry:
      max_attempts: 5
spruce:
  region: eu
  plan: free
  suspended: true
  overrides:
    retention:
      audit_days: 3
    service:
      request_timeout_ms: 1200

## config/regions.yaml

eu:
  deployment_region: eu-west-2
  audit_bucket: harbor-prod-eu-audit
  export_bucket: harbor-prod-eu-exports
  attachment_bucket: harbor-prod-eu-files
  metrics_prefix: hd.eu
us:
  deployment_region: us-central-1
  audit_bucket: harbor-prod-us-audit
  export_bucket: harbor-prod-us-exports
  attachment_bucket: harbor-prod-us-files
  metrics_prefix: hd.us

Audit records go to regions[tenant.region].audit_bucket. Export objects go to the export_bucket in the same region. Attachments use attachment_bucket. The deployment_region string is metadata, not a key into a second routing table. Bucket names are logical names in this fixture and cannot be contacted.

## config/plans.yaml

free:
  max_inflight: 3
  monthly_export_limit: 10
  attachment_limit_mb: 5
team:
  max_inflight: 8
  monthly_export_limit: 100
  attachment_limit_mb: 25
pro:
  max_inflight: 12
  monthly_export_limit: 500
  attachment_limit_mb: 50

A tenant's general-worker concurrency limit is plans[tenant.plan].max_inflight. The optional export worker has its own fixed concurrency of 2 and does not change the general-worker limit. The monthly export limit is a billing counter, not a concurrency setting. A suspended tenant remains in the configuration but cannot dispatch new work.

## src/dispatch.py

def classify_ticket(score, tier, flagged):
    if flagged:
        return "quarantine"
    if tier == "free" and score >= 90:
        return "manual"
    if score >= 80:
        return "priority"
    return "standard"

def webhook_enabled(tenant, effective_config):
    return effective_config["features"]["webhooks"] and not tenant["suspended"]

def route_for(classification, effective_config):
    if classification == "manual":
        return "tickets.manual-review"
    return effective_config["queues"][classification]

The classifier returns a classification, not a queue name. route_for runs afterward. Scores are numbers on a 0–100 scale with no rounding. Webhook enablement is independent of audit.

## src/retry.py

def retry_delays(max_attempts, initial_delay_s, multiplier):
    return [
        initial_delay_s * (multiplier ** i)
        for i in range(max_attempts - 1)
    ]

The caller waits after each failed call except the last. There is no initial wait, jitter, or final wait. If every attempt fails, each returned delay is used once. Execution time is separate from waiting time.

## src/ingest.py

def split_batches(items, max_chunk_items):
    return [
        items[start:start + max_chunk_items]
        for start in range(0, len(items), max_chunk_items)
    ]

def canonical_path(path):
    while path != "/" and path.endswith("/"):
        path = path[:-1]
    return path

Batching retains the final partial batch and neither filters nor duplicates items. canonical_path only removes trailing slashes while preserving a root slash; it does not decode URLs or change internal slashes.

## src/http.py

def timeout_for(route, effective_config):
    if route == "/readyz":
        return effective_config["service"]["health_timeout_ms"]
    if route.startswith("/exports/"):
        return 9000
    return effective_config["service"]["request_timeout_ms"]

The caller passes the canonical path to timeout_for. Health checks use /readyz. Export paths use the fixed timeout in this function. Other paths inherit request_timeout_ms from the merged configuration. The selected timeout is an integer number of milliseconds; this function does not start a timer or perform network I/O.

## docs/operations.md — reference notes

The dashboard warns after three missed heartbeat intervals; that threshold is not the interval. A developer reverse proxy can listen on 9443, but it is outside production. Audit retention is independent of local logs. The billing export limit is not a concurrency limit. Paid plans do not automatically enable webhooks. Export workers start only for export jobs.

## tests/test_settings.py — test-only overrides

TEST_SETTINGS = {
    "service": {"listen_port": 9090, "request_timeout_ms": 50},
    "worker": {"heartbeat_interval_s": 1},
    "retention": {"audit_days": 1},
    "upload": {"max_chunk_items": 4},
}

These test values are injected by the unit-test runner only. None are used by the production snapshot.

## archive/production-0.6.yaml — inactive historical example

  listen_port: 9443
worker:
  heartbeat_interval_s: 20
retention:
  audit_days: 14
queues:
  priority: tickets.high
retry:
  max_attempts: 3
upload:
  max_chunk_items: 8

The historical file is inactive. No queue aliases are defined. Questions concern the active snapshot unless they explicitly name an archived or test file.
